traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 372 Liliaceae (wide sense, which held the lilies, Melanthiaceae, Colchicaceae and Smilacaceae of APG's Liliales): perianth of six segments in two whorls, mostly alike (petal-like tepals); Trillium and its kin have green sepals and coloured petals. The ovary is superior in most; Alstroemeriaceae, also in the order, have it inferior.

traits.flowering_position.note: APweb Liliales page (read 2026-10-16): inflorescence terminal (order character). Smilacaceae overridden.

traits.life_span.note: Wikipedia Liliales (read 2026-10-16): mostly perennial bulbous, rhizomatous or cormous geophytes, some climbers and shrubs; DELTA Smilacaceae (read 2026-10-16): perennial.

traits.leaf_habit.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): order of geophytes (leafy shoots die back after flowering); DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Smilacaceae leaves persistent, which it states. Weighting inferred.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): Petermanniaceae and Alstroemerieae spiral, Luzuriageae two-ranked, Colchicaceae two-ranked or spiral, Corsiaceae spiral to two-ranked. Liliaceae (largest family) spirally leaved (our reading).

traits.rosette.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): leaves mostly on the flowering stem in Liliaceae (Lilium, Fritillaria) and Smilacaceae climbers; basal leaves in Erythronium, some Melanthiaceae. Weighting inferred.

traits.inflorescence.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): Melanthiaceae raceme or panicle, Liliaceae racemose or scapose, Colchicaceae racemose or single flowers, Smilacaceae umbels (states its own).

traits.sexual_system.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): Melanthiaceae mostly bisexual, Chamaelirium dioecious; Wikipedia Smilacaceae (read 2026-10-16): dioecious (states its own).

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb Liliales page (read 2026-10-16): tepals free, each with a nectary; no floral cup.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): monosymmetry where it occurs (Alstroemerieae, Gloriosa, Corsiaceae) is by tepal shape or curvature; no labellum/bilabiate pattern except Corsiaceae's odd tepal.
